svg.title: A simulated null distribution beside the model curve
svg.desc: Two panels on the same horizontal axis. On the left, a histogram of 1000 simulated sample rates centred on 0.80 with the bars at or below 0.74 shaded. On the right, a smooth bell curve over the same faint histogram with the same left tail shaded.
svg.text: Same question, two ways to find the tail
sample on-time rate if the claim is true
sample on-time rate if the claim is true
Week 12: draw the model, then read the area
the same axis, relabelled in standard units (z)
Both tails point at the same conclusion: a rate this low turns up in roughly two samples in a hundred when the
advertised claim holds. The curve is a model of the shuffling, so the two areas agree closely but not exactly.
